name: DC Hub
description: Data centre and power-grid intelligence from DC Hub: 22,900+ facilities across 170 countries, market power-readiness scores, the US interconnection queue, construction pipeline, M&A transactions, live ISO grid fuel mix and electricity prices, plus site scoring and multi-site ranking. Most tools work without an API key.
instructions:
Data centre and energy-grid intelligence for site selection, infrastructure investment and power analysis.

## Credentials are optional
Most tools answer without any key, so you can install this connector and start asking questions immediately. Two things need one:
- `dchub_facility_detail` (the full record for a single facility, including contacts and certifications)
- `dchub_grid_fuel_mix` (live ISO fuel mix)

To get a key: DC Hub hands out a free developer key from a single POST to `https://dchub.cloud/api/v1/keys/claim` with `{"client_name": "<your name>"}` — no email, no browser. It allows **10 requests/day**, which is enough to try things and not enough to work with; real use needs a paid DC Hub plan (https://dchub.cloud/pricing). Paste the key into `DCHUB_API_KEY` in this connector's settings and every tool starts using it.

## Where to start
- **"Is market X a good place to build?"** → `dchub_market_dcpi` with a market slug (`phoenix`, `northern-virginia`, `dallas`). It returns a BUILD / CAUTION / AVOID verdict, a composite score, an excess-power score, a constraint score and time-to-power in months. `dchub_compare_markets` puts several side by side, `dchub_list_markets` tells you which slugs exist.
- **"Where is there power soon?"** → `dchub_ai_capacity_index` ranks markets by AI-ready deployable MW over a 30/60/90-day horizon.
- **"Find me sites"** → `dchub_interconnection_queue` filters ~5,300 US interconnection-queue projects server-side (by MW, ISO, fuel, time-to-power, fibre distance). Ask for `geocoded_only: true` and you get rows with coordinates you can feed straight into `dchub_site_score` or `dchub_rank_sites`.
- **"Score this specific place"** → `dchub_site_score` takes a lat/lon. `dchub_analyze_parcel` takes a GeoJSON polygon and returns geodesic acreage, a representative point and a contiguity flag.
- **"Rank my shortlist"** → `dchub_rank_sites` is a deterministic optimiser: hard constraints as `{field: {min, max}}`, objectives as `{field: signedWeight}` where a positive weight maximises and a negative one minimises.

## Reading the data
- Capacity is in MW throughout. `time_to_power_months` is an ISO-level average interconnection wait, not a promise for a specific project.
- ISO codes are `PJM`, `ERCOT`, `MISO`, `CAISO`, `SPP`, `NYISO`, `ISO-NE` (the fuel-mix tool spells the last one `ISONE`).
- The interconnection queue defaults to `status: active`, which excludes withdrawn, cancelled, suspended and already-commercial projects. Pass a different status only if you specifically want those.
- `baseload_only: true` keeps firm and dispatchable fuel and drops wind, solar and storage. It is a firm/intermittent split, nothing finer.
- Electricity prices are US-state-level (`dchub_energy_prices` takes a two-letter state abbreviation).

## Scope, honestly
This connector wraps DC Hub's 16 public REST endpoints. DC Hub also runs its own MCP server with more tools than these. The reason to use this one is that it sits in the same workspace, credentials and permission model as everything else you have connected — not that it is more complete.

Read-only apart from the two POST analysis tools, which compute and return a result without storing anything.

tools.name: dchub_stats
tools.description: Platform-wide statistics: total facilities tracked, countries, providers and aggregate capacity in MW. No API key needed. Useful as a first call to see the shape of the dataset.

tools.name: dchub_search_facilities
tools.description: Search 22,900+ data centre facilities by free text (city, provider or market name) and/or country. Returns summary records. Use dchub_facility_detail with an id from here for the full record (that one needs an API key).

q.description: Search term: a city, a provider name or a market, e.g. 'Equinix Frankfurt'.

tools.name: dchub_facility_detail
tools.description: Full record for one facility: contacts, capacity detail and certifications. REQUIRES an API key (DCHUB_API_KEY) — without one this returns 403. Get the facility_id from dchub_search_facilities.

facility_id.description: Numeric facility id, as returned by dchub_search_facilities.

tools.name: dchub_list_markets
tools.description: List every tracked data centre market with summary statistics. Call this first to learn the market slugs that dchub_market_dcpi and dchub_compare_markets expect.

tools.name: dchub_compare_markets
tools.description: Side-by-side comparison of two or more data centre markets. Pass the market names comma-separated.

tools.name: dchub_market_dcpi
tools.description: DC Hub Power Index for one market: a BUILD / CAUTION / AVOID verdict plus composite_score, excess_power_score, constraint_score and time_to_power_months. Recomputed daily. The single most useful tool for 'should we build here?'.

market_slug.description: Market slug, e.g. 'phoenix', 'northern-virginia', 'dallas'. Get valid slugs from dchub_list_markets.

tools.name: dchub_ai_capacity_index
tools.description: Markets ranked by AI-ready deployable MW for near-term large-load siting, with a hyperscale_ready flag and an ai_ready_mw proxy. Answers 'where can a big AI load actually land in the next 30/60/90 days?'.

tools.name: dchub_interconnection_queue
tools.description: Filter the ~5,300-project US interconnection queue (7 ISOs) server-side, so you receive the survivors instead of the raw ~1,744 GW queue. This is the site-sourcing tool: combine min_mw, iso, fuel and time-to-power filters, then set geocoded_only to get rows with coordinates you can pass to dchub_site_score or dchub_rank_sites.

min_mw.description: Minimum project capacity in MW, e.g. 1000 for 1 GW and above.

max_ttp_months.description: Max time-to-power in months; keeps projects in ISOs at or under this average interconnection wait.

iso.description: One or more ISOs, comma-separated union, from PJM, ERCOT, MISO, CAISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE.

baseload_only.description: Keep only firm/dispatchable fuel and drop wind, solar and storage (default false).

fuel_type.description: Inclusive substring match on the raw fuel label; comma or semicolon separated for a union, e.g. 'gas' matches GAS and Natural Gas.

status.description: Queue status filter. Default 'active' = still progressing, excluding withdrawn, cancelled, suspended and in-commercial-operation.

max_fiber_km.description: Keep only survivors within this many km of the nearest mapped long-haul fibre route endpoint (coarse backbone data).

geocoded_only.description: Keep only survivors carrying lat/lng (~83% of the queue) — the ones you can pipe into parcel analysis or site scoring (default false).

tools.name: dchub_pipeline
tools.description: Data centres under construction or announced — the forward supply picture for a market.

tools.name: dchub_transactions
tools.description: Recent data centre M&A: acquisitions, investments, joint ventures, leases and development deals.

deal_type.description: One of: acquisition, investment, joint_venture, lease, development.

tools.name: dchub_news
tools.description: Latest data centre industry news, aggregated from 40+ sources.

tools.name: dchub_site_score
tools.description: Suitability score (0-100) for data centre development at one specific location. Pass coordinates; the US state abbreviation sharpens the energy side of the score.

tools.name: dchub_grid_fuel_mix
tools.description: Real-time fuel mix of a US power grid, refreshed about every 60 seconds. REQUIRES an API key (DCHUB_API_KEY) — without one this returns 403 with instructions for claiming a free developer key.

iso.description: Grid operator: ERCOT, PJM, CAISO, MISO, SPP, NYISO or ISONE.

tools.name: dchub_energy_prices
tools.description: Electricity pricing for one US state — the input to any operating-cost estimate for a site in that state.

tools.name: dchub_analyze_parcel
tools.description: Structured read of a GeoJSON parcel boundary: geodesic acreage, the largest member's centroid as a representative point (never the centre of a multi-part shape), a contiguity flag, a per-member breakdown and a site-evaluation handoff object you can carry into dchub_rank_sites. Computes and returns; stores nothing.

geometry.description: GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon describing the parcel boundary.

capacity_mw.description: Optional target load in MW, carried into the handoff object.

tools.name: dchub_rank_sites
tools.description: Deterministic ranking of candidate sites under hard constraints and signed weighted objectives. Constraints fail closed: a candidate missing a constrained field is dropped. A positive objective weight maximises that field, a negative one minimises it. Computes and returns; stores nothing.

candidates.description: Pre-enriched candidates: [{id?, lat?, lng?, <metric fields>}]. Carry through any site_evaluation_handoff from dchub_analyze_parcel.

constraints.description: Hard filters as {field: {min?, max?}}. A candidate missing the field is dropped.

objectives.description: {field: signedWeight} — a positive weight maximises the field, a negative one minimises it.

absolute.description: Score on a fixed 0-100 scale that is stable across runs, instead of min-max within this batch.

percentile.description: Score as a percentile against the viable-site population. Takes precedence over absolute.

top_k.description: How many ranked sites to return (default 3).
